name: nandwright
displayName: Nandwright: Nand2Tetris IDE (HDL, Hack Assembly, VM, Jack)
description: Run, test and debug every Nand2Tetris project inside VS Code: hardware simulator and live circuit diagrams for HDL chips, test scripts (.tst) in the Testing view, Hack assembler and CPU emulator, VM emulator, Jack compiler, screen and keyboard. No Java, nothing else to install.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Nothing course-specific: you choose the zip's name, folders and files with the `nandwright.zip` settings.

KTH EP121U (Computer Science): projects 1 to 4 are the book's folders `01`+`02`, `03`, `04` and `05`; zips are named `Project01-familyname-firstname.zip` (`project09-…` for project 9); only the files the course asks for are ticked, plus the project's grade sheet.
nandwright.course.markdownDescription: Hand-in rules of your course for **Zip Project for Hand-In**. A setting you set yourself (`#nandwright.zip.fileName#`, `#nandwright.zip.projects#`) wins over the course's. Run **Nand2Tetris: Set Up…** to choose.

nandwright.student.familyName.markdownDescription: Your family name, for `{familyname}` in `#nandwright.zip.fileName#`. Kept in your user settings only.

nandwright.student.firstName.markdownDescription: Your first name, for `{firstname}` in `#nandwright.zip.fileName#`. Kept in your user settings only.

nandwright.circuit.animate.markdownDescription: In the circuit diagram, light up the wires whose value changed after an input change or a clock step, in the order the signal travels. Off when your system asks for reduced motion. The diagram's Animate button sets this too.

nandwright.simulator.followEditor.markdownDescription: Open chip simulators and circuit diagrams follow the active `.hdl` file. The Hack computer and VM emulator follow the active `.asm`, `.hack`, `.vm` or `.jack` file. Turn this off to keep separate panels fixed to the files they were opened for.

nandwright.test.pressKeys.markdownDescription: When a test script waits for a key (the official project 5 `Memory.tst` asks you to hold down `K`), press that key for it. Turn this off to press the keys yourself in the chip panel, as you would in the official Hardware Simulator.

nandwright.test.runOnSave.markdownDescription: Run a file's tests when you save it: saving a chip, a program, a test script or a compare file runs the test scripts in the same folder that use it. Results appear in the Testing view and in the simulator panel without taking focus. Scripts that repeat forever are not run this way.

nandwright.test.buildSources.markdownDescription: When a test script loads a `.hack` or `.vm` file (such as project 4's `Mult.tst` and `FillAutomatic.tst`, or project 12's OS tests), assemble the `.asm` or compile the `.jack` source in memory when the built file is missing, older than the source, or being edited. Never writes `.hack` or `.vm` files to disk.

nandwright.zip.fileName.markdownDescription: The name **Zip Project for Hand-In** offers for the zip, without `.zip`. `{folder}` is the folder's name. `{n}` is the project's number: its key in `#nandwright.zip.projects#` if the folder is listed there, otherwise the number in the folder's name without leading zeros (`01` gives `1`). `{nn}` is that number with two digits (`1` gives `01`). `{familyname}` and `{firstname}` are your name from `#nandwright.student.familyName#` and `#nandwright.student.firstName#`; if one is not set, you are asked when you zip. Example: `Project{nn}-{familyname}-{firstname}`. Leave it unset to use your course preset's name, or the folder's name.

nandwright.zip.projects.markdownDescription: For courses that number their projects differently from the folders, or hand in several folders as one project. Each key is a project number as your course counts it; its value lists the folders of that project. Example: `{ "1": ["01", "02"], "2": ["03"] }`. Zipping folder `01` or `02` then packs both folders into one zip, and `{n}` is `1`; zipping `03` gives project `2`. A name is a folder next to the one you zip; a name with `/` is a path inside the workspace folder. Folders that are not listed are zipped on their own, as before.

nandwright.zip.gradeSheetFolder.markdownDescription: The folder where you keep your grade sheets, if it is not a folder named `grade-sheets`. A path inside the workspace folder, or a full path. The zip takes the sheet for the project's number from it, such as `Project1.xlsx` or `project_01.ods`.

nandwright.trace.server.description: Trace the communication with the language server in the Output panel. For reporting bugs.

script.description: The .tst test script to step through.

walkthroughs.title: Nand2Tetris in VS Code
walkthroughs.description: From an empty chip to a passing test, without leaving the editor.

steps.title: Open your nand2tetris folder
steps.description:
Open the folder that holds the course's ``projects`` folder (or any folder with ``.hdl`` and ``.tst`` files). You do not need the ``tools`` folder or Java.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)
[Try the example chip instead](command:nandwright.openExample)

steps.title: Write a chip
steps.description: Open a ``.hdl`` file and fill in its ``PARTS:`` section. Completion suggests chips and their pins, hover shows each chip's interface, and mistakes are underlined as you type. An empty chip is not an error: it is where every project starts.

steps.title: Run its test
steps.description:
Press the play button at the top right of the editor, or use the Testing view to run a whole project. The result matches the official Hardware Simulator.
[Run the test of the open chip](command:nandwright.runTest)

steps.title: See why a test fails
steps.description:
A failing test shows the expected and actual rows side by side, with the value of every internal pin at that step. Open the chip in the simulator, draw its live circuit diagram, or step through the test script line by line.
[Open the chip in the simulator](command:nandwright.openChip)
[Show circuit diagram](command:nandwright.showCircuit)

steps.title: Run programs on the Hack computer
steps.description:
From project 4 on you write programs: Hack assembly, VM code, Jack. Run them with the screen and keyboard, pause at breakpoints, and inspect registers and memory.
[Run the open program](command:nandwright.runProgram)

steps.title: Set up handing in
steps.description:
Choose your course, type your name and show where your grade sheets are. Then **Zip Project for Hand-In** names the zip, picks the files and adds the grade sheet.
[Set Up](command:nandwright.setup)
